full_script:
Friday morning. The yard is already open. Taeo and Nib arrive together at the equipment bench. Taeo takes the folded assessment sheet from his jacket and gives it to Minho. Nib watches a worker finish placing a screen in the distance.

MINHO: Morning. You're on time.

TAEO: You asked me to bring this.

No journey recap, greeting montage or new introduction.

dialogue.text: You asked me to bring this.

full_script:
Minho reads the sheet once, folds it along its existing crease, and returns it. Taeo puts it in his inside jacket pocket before anything else is handed out. The writing is not framed for reading.

MINHO: Keep it with you. We're only working in the yard.

Minho turns to Nib with the ochre radio in his hand.

MINHO: Same button as yesterday.

dialogue.text: Keep it with you. We're only working in the yard.

full_script:
Nib takes the radio in his LEFT hand. Minho points toward the newly arranged screens; Taeo stays by the bench, clear of working traffic.

MINHO: Walk the new route. Tell me anything the crew will need moved before they start.

NIB: All right.

This is the agreed paid ground check, not a test for an announced rank. No promise of expertise with modern machines.

dialogue.text: Walk the new route. Tell me anything the crew will need moved before they start.

full_script:
Low, honest view from Nib's position in the north–south passage. At its eastward turn, a loose loop of cord lies across the exit. One end leads to an unused coil beside the outer face of the screen. Nib stops before it. His size does not confer supernatural detection; it is simply visible when he reaches the turn.

Nib presses the radio button.

NIB, RADIO: There's cord across the way out. By the last screen.

dialogue.text: There's cord across the way out. By the last screen.

full_script:
At the exit apron, Minho crouches and gathers the loose cord toward its coil, clearing the entire walking line. Nib stands in the passage, radio lowered in his left hand, free right hand indicating the affected stretch. Nobody steps into a tightening loop.

MINHO: This one?

NIB: Yes. It goes round the foot there, too.

The cord's short wrap around the screen support foot is plainly visible. Minho lifts the loose loop clear by hand; no screen moves or collapses.

dialogue.text: Yes. It goes round the foot there, too.

full_script:
Compact time-passage composition: later in the same hour, Nib returns along the exterior of a different screen toward the bench. The new route is now clear. Minho and an ordinary crew member walk it at adult height before opening it for use. Taeo watches from the same bench apron. Morning light has moved slightly.

No dialogue. This closes ordinary checks economically. Do not add a montage of hidden hazards, ten discoveries or a score screen. Nib has performed a modest supervised job, and the crew checks its own equipment.

At the bench, Minho checks his watch: nine. Keep this an ordinary glance, not a giant clock insert. Nib places the radio into Minho's waiting hand. Minho puts it in the charging rack.

MINHO: That's the hour. Thanks.

Nib flexes his now-empty left hand once. He has been walking, not battling exhaustion.

Minho takes two ten-thousand-won notes from a small payment envelope and holds them down where Nib can take them comfortably. Nib takes both with his right hand. Taeo stays out of the exchange.

MINHO: Twenty thousand. As agreed.

NIB: Both of these?

MINHO: Both.

Payment is completed here. No bank account, ownership law or payroll scene is introduced.

Nib folds the notes once and places them in his right-hip pouch beside, not inside, his separately folded original sketch. He reties the pouch.

Taeo's expression is pleased, with a trace of envy he does not announce. The job was Nib's. He has watched rather than quietly been promoted to operator.

NIB, TO MINHO: Where is your crew going next?

dialogue.text: Where is your crew going next?

full_script:
Minho indicates a crew member loading a closed equipment case into an ordinary parked van beyond the screens. He stays with the visitors at the bench.

MINHO: A drainage tunnel. They're surveying it this afternoon.

NIB: Underground?

MINHO: All the section we're checking.

An actual answer to the question promised at the end of Chapter 6. No claim that every route in that dungeon is known. The van is equipment transport, not a portal or a mission invitation.

dialogue.text: A drainage tunnel. They're surveying it this afternoon.

full_script:
Nib takes out and unfolds his original watch-post sketch. Minho recognizes the same paper from yesterday, rather than pretending to see it for the first time.

NIB: So they won't see this.

MINHO: Not on that survey.

He looks at the wall and tree once, without an uncanny recognition reaction.

Taeo takes his phone from his jacket. Nib folds the sketch and holds it in his RIGHT hand; the left is free.

TAEO: We're looking through the recordings Chae sent.

NIB: If I find it in one, can you go there?

Nib asks Minho. It is a practical question about access, not a declaration that he comes from a dungeon.

dialogue.text: We're looking through the recordings Chae sent.
If I find it in one, can you go there?

full_script:
Taeo opens the link himself. Minho points to the screen from beside him, without taking the device.

MINHO: If the gate's still open. Which recordings?

TAEO: These.

No new app, search expertise or completed archive work is implied. Taeo reopens the same six-item link.

dialogue.text: If the gate's still open. Which recordings?

full_script:
Taeo selects the first recording, recognizable by its forked pale boulder thumbnail. This is the one Nib was mapping in Chapter 5. The video is paused. Minho points beneath the picture, where a small details row can be expanded.

MINHO: Open that.

Taeo taps with his right thumb. His left supports the phone.

Medium three-shot, not another screen close-up. Minho looks at the newly visible entry details.

MINHO: This gate's closed.

Taeo's thumb stops. Nib looks up from the paper in his hand.

NIB: But the picture's still there.

Native phone image close-up: the familiar paused forked boulder above a clean, restrained physical webpage details area. Exact readable text, no other mandatory labels:

GATE STATUS: CLOSED
Recording retained

MINHO, OFF PANEL: The recording stays. The gate doesn't.

This is an ordinary archive fact plus the already established boss-clear closure rule. It does not establish that a closed landscape is destroyed, that it can never be reached again, that Nib came through this gate, or that all six entries are closed.

dialogue.text: The recording stays. The gate doesn't.

full_script:
Nib unfolds his original sketch with both hands again and holds it beside the phone in Taeo's hands, keeping the two pictures separate. The boulder and the watch-post drawing plainly do not match. The small status row remains consistent with P16 if visible. No ghostly superimposition, matching symbol or magic pulse.

TAEO: We could start with the ones still open.

NIB: Yes. Keep this one, though.

dialogue.text: We could start with the ones still open.

full_script:
Nib refolds his sketch. His gaze stays on the physical paper rather than the status line.

NIB: If my wall's in an old picture, I still want to know.

TAEO: Okay.

He is not discarding useful evidence just because it is no longer an entrance. No renewed promise to solve everything.

dialogue.text: If my wall's in an old picture, I still want to know.

full_script:
Minho turns at a colleague's call from the loading area. The working morning resumes. Nib puts his sketch in the pouch and reties it. Taeo locks and pockets the phone.

COLLEAGUE, OFF PANEL: Minho. Can you check this strap?

MINHO: Coming.

To Nib, briefly:

MINHO: Thanks for this morning.

No automatic second job, recruitment offer or future clue is tacked onto the goodbye.

dialogue.text: Minho. Can you check this strap?

full_script:
Outside the yard, walking along the same ordinary pavement as Chapter 6. Taeo looks down toward Nib; Nib has been feeling the folded banknotes through the pouch cloth, then drops his hand.

TAEO: Hungry?

NIB: Yes.

Warm cooking steam drifts from an open noodle shop ahead. The image supplies their next destination; no speculative meal-shopping montage.

Inside the shop entrance at the order counter. Two plain sample food photographs are mounted low enough for Nib to see. Nib indicates the noodle bowl. Taeo stands beside him, not between him and the server.

NIB: How much is that one?

The server starts to answer Taeo, catches that Nib asked, and redirects their gaze down. One contained beat.

SERVER: Seven thousand won.

Nib takes out his two folded notes, separates ONE ten-thousand-won note, and returns the other to the pouch before holding out payment in his right hand. Taeo has not reached for his wallet yet.

NIB: One.

TAEO: You don't have to—

NIB: I'm buying mine.

Matter-of-fact, not a rejection of shared meals or repayment of a moral debt. Taeo lets the unfinished offer go.

The server puts three one-thousand-won notes on a low change tray within Nib's reach. Nib gathers them; Taeo points to the three notes without taking them.

TAEO: Three thousand back.

NIB: Right.

Nib puts the change into his pouch and reties it with both hands now empty. This is one small purchase, not a literacy or arithmetic tutorial. His balance is now thirteen thousand won.

A compact transition to their low table: two bowls have arrived. Taeo has paid for his own bowl during the ordinary cut; neither bowl is charged to Nib twice. Taeo's shoes sit on the entrance ledge. Both sit on floor cushions. Nib can comfortably reach the rim of a full-sized bowl from his adult seated position; no oversized head or toy serving set.

Nib tastes the broth from an ordinary spoon and immediately takes another spoonful. Taeo is separating his noodles. No dialogue. Let earning and buying something have a moment of pleasure.

Taeo's phone vibrates inside his jacket lying folded beside his cushion. He retrieves it, looks at a message and places it screen-down beside his own bowl, outside spill range. No readable phone inset is needed.

TAEO: Grandma wants to know when I'll get there Sunday.

NIB: How long will you be gone?

TAEO: Most of the day.

This does not cancel Saturday work or silently establish that Nib can remain at arbitrary distance.

dialogue.text: Grandma wants to know when I'll get there Sunday.
How long will you be gone?

full_script:
Nib puts his spoon in his own bowl, then looks up at Taeo.

NIB: Can I come?

Taeo's expression opens with surprise rather than relief at obedience.

TAEO: If you'd like. I'll ask her.

Nib has chosen to ask. There is no forced accompaniment, claim of tested range, or speech about found family.

dialogue.text: If you'd like. I'll ask her.

full_script:
Taeo lifts the phone again, places a voice call to his grandmother, and holds it to his RIGHT ear. Nib resumes eating. Restaurant background stays subdued; Taeo speaks quietly enough for an ordinary table call. No video, family model redesign or new handset UI is required.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: Taeo?

TAEO: Noon on Sunday, if that's okay.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: That's fine.

dialogue.text: Noon on Sunday, if that's okay.

full_script:
Taeo looks toward Nib, who is listening while holding his spoon above the bowl.

TAEO: Can I bring someone?

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: Who?

TAEO: His name's Nib. He's staying with me.

He has not called Nib a pet, child, friend of long standing or employee.

dialogue.text: His name's Nib. He's staying with me.

full_script:
Taeo lowers his voice a little further, shoulders drawing in.

TAEO: I awakened this week. I summoned him.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: You what?

The sharp, ordinary family surprise is about news he failed to tell her. Give the reaction room without a comedy distortion.

dialogue.text: I awakened this week. I summoned him.

full_script:
Taeo glances at the busy restaurant, then down at his own bowl.

TAEO: I'm all right. I went to the assessment office.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: Why didn't you tell me?

TAEO: I didn't know how to explain it.

He does not claim the assessment is a field license, that he is strong, or that his grandmother knows the gate incident's details already.

dialogue.text: I'm all right. I went to the assessment office.
I didn't know how to explain it.

full_script:
Taeo listens rather than defending the delay. Nib sets his spoon in his bowl and stops eating.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: You can explain it on Sunday. Are you going into gates?

TAEO: No.

A clean, truthful answer about his current intention and activity. No oath that he can never change, future career announcement or cure for his fear.

dialogue.text: You can explain it on Sunday. Are you going into gates?

full_script:
Taeo turns his face toward Nib so the next sentence includes the person concerned.

TAEO: Nib's a goblin. He talks. He asked if he could come.

A brief silence from the phone.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: He asked you?

TAEO: Yes.

Her surprise is allowed. Do not turn sentient summons into something this family has always known.

dialogue.text: Nib's a goblin. He talks. He asked if he could come.

full_script:
Taeo still holds the phone to his ear. Nib hears only Taeo's side and waits; do not give him magical hearing of the remote voice.

GRANDMOTHER, PHONE: All right. Does he eat fish?

TAEO, TO NIB: Do you eat fish?

NIB: Yes.

TAEO, INTO PHONE: He does.

A compact back-and-forth. No phone is passed over food; no unintroduced speakerphone setting. The invitation follows the question Nib chose to ask.

dialogue.text: All right. Does he eat fish?

full_script:
Final generous two-shot at the low table. The call has ended and Taeo sets the phone screen-down beside his bowl again. Nib picks up his spoon. Their food is still warm; the conversation took a short minute, not the whole meal.

TAEO: Both of us. Noon.

NIB: Then eat. Yours is going cold.

Taeo looks at his untouched noodles, then starts eating. Nib's pouch rests at his right hip, holding his remaining money and his separate old drawing. No explanatory caption, loyalty declaration, new message, hidden landscape match or looming monster.

dialogue.text: Then eat. Yours is going cold.
